title: Evaluation of targeted and high-resolution mass spectrometry methods for environmental monitoring of pharmaceuticals
author: Golovko, Sörengård, et al.

steps.title: Filter water samples
steps.instruction: Take seven replicate 10 mL aliquots of each thawed wastewater or surface‑water sample and filter them through 0.45 µm regenerated‑cellulose syringe filters (Labicom, Olomouc, Czech Republic).

steps.title: Spike internal standard
steps.instruction: Add the internal‑standard (IS) mixture to each filtered sample to achieve a final concentration of 50 ng L⁻¹.

steps.title: Online SPE‑LC processing
steps.instruction: Process the IS‑spiked samples using the online solid‑phase extraction coupled with liquid chromatography (on‑line SPE‑LC) method as described in references [11,12].

steps.title: Prepare calibration curves
steps.instruction: Prepare calibration standards in ultrapure water covering 1–1000 ng L⁻¹ for river water (RW) and tap water (TW) matrices and 1–10 000 ng L⁻¹ for influent (IW) and effluent (EW) matrices; measure a calibration curve at the beginning and at the end of each analytical sequence to monitor instrument stability.

steps.title: Define limits of quantification
steps.instruction: Define the LOQ as the 14 % of the lowest calibration point whose relative standard deviation (RSD) of the average response factor is <30 %; determine individual LOQs from the signal intensity at that concentration.

steps.title: Assess trueness by spiking
steps.instruction: Spike separate aliquots of each matrix at the following levels: TW – 10 ng L⁻¹ and 100 ng L⁻¹; RW – 50 ng L⁻¹ and 500 ng L⁻¹; IW and EW – 500 ng L⁻¹, 1000 ng L⁻¹ and 5000 ng L⁻¹. Calculate trueness using the formula: Trueness (%) = (Peakarea₍pre‑spiked₎ − Peakarea₍Blank₎) / (Peakarea₍post‑spiked₎ − Peakarea₍Blank₎) × 100.

steps.title: Prepare matrix‑matched standards
steps.instruction: Prepare matrix‑matched calibration standards (MST) by spiking internal standards at 50 ng L⁻¹ and native analytes at matrix‑specific concentrations: 5000 ng L⁻¹ for IW and EW, 100 ng L⁻¹ for RW, and 50 ng L⁻¹ for TW.

steps.title: Calculate matrix effects
steps.instruction: Calculate the matrix‑affected response factor as the difference between the peak‑area‑to‑IS ratio in matrix‑matched standards and non‑spiked samples, then compute Matrix effects (%) = (Peakarea₍MST₎ − Peakarea₍Blank₎) / Peakarea₍Solvent₎ × 100.

steps.title: Evaluate precision and blanks
steps.instruction: Measure each analyte in seven replicates of the sample matrix and calculate the relative standard deviation (RSD) to assess precision. Prepare tap‑water blanks (n = 3) and ultrapure‑water blanks (n = 3) and analyze them under identical conditions; confirm that no target compounds are detected.
